gen_risks.description: Involvement of multiple line ministries and agencies across project components may cause institutional coordination friction and implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a Ministerial Coordination Committee under the Minister of Labor and utilize a restructured PIU shared with SPRRP.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.B Financial Management: ...delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders...

gen_risks.description: Public TVET institutions face capacity constraints due to outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, operating deficits, and instructor gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide direct financial compensation for training delivery costs, procure modern equipment, and rehabilitate existing facilities through AFAP.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.B Sectoral Context: ...capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps...

gen_risks.description: Construction of the US$5 million training center on Príncipe faces severe logistical constraints, cost risks, and delays due to geographic insularity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure detailed technical designs early, enforce EDGE Level 1 green building standards, and manage budget adjustments through procurement plan revisions.
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D Subcomponent 1.1: ...structural constraints specific to Príncipe—including geographic isolation and a severely limited pool of skilled workers...

gen_risks.description: Financial management bottlenecks at AFAP, including transaction recording delays and late internal audit reviews, could impede project disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated financial management accountant, customize accounting software, and update the financial procedures in the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.B Financial Management: FM risks identified include: (i) delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports; (ii) internal audit reviews...

gen_risks.description: Delays in MLSSS providing technical inputs and specifications to AFAP could stall procurement of civil works, goods, and key consultancies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal workflow protocols between MLSSS technical leads and AFAP fiduciary specialists, detailed in the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.B Procurement: A key factor for good procurement performance will be the ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration...

gen_risks.description: Delays or non-compliance in beneficiary selection criteria could interrupt cash stipend and sub-grant transfers for youth and MSMEs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract a qualified electronic Payment Service Provider and satisfy formal disbursement conditions prior to sub-grant and stipend releases.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.B Financial Management: ...delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria.

gen_risks.description: Vulnerable youth outside the capital or unindexed in databases face potential exclusion and elite capture during project beneficiary selection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize objective socio-economic data from the Unique Social Registry, enforce geographic quotas, and operationalize a project Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C ESF: ...risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... as well as risks of elite capture...

gen_risks.description: Female participants in training centers, internships, and work placements face risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated Social Specialist with GBV/SEA-SH expertise and enforce code-of-conduct and safety mechanisms across participating training centers and employers.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C ESF: ...community health and safety risks, including risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH)...

gen_risks.description: Micro-enterprise grants and facility rehabilitation works could generate solid waste, construction debris, or cause localized environmental degradation in sensitive ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an Environmental Specialist, mandate environmental screening for MSME sub-grants, and enforce environmental management guidelines for civil works.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C ESF: ...small business grants could support micro-enterprises in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism that may indirectly place pressure on sensitive ecosystems...

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting core PIU technical staff (TVET specialist, IT assistant, E&S specialists) could overburden existing staff and slow component rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce legal covenants mandating the appointment of key specialists within 45 to 60 days of project effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal Covenants: The Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire or appoint, not later than sixty (60) days after Effectiveness: (i) a TVET specialist...

gen_risks.description: Recurrent flooding, storms, and sea-level rise could disrupt training activities, delay infrastructure works, and impact beneficiary livelihoods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate-resilient engineering standards for physical works, install backup generators, and incorporate flexible training schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C Assessment of adaptation risks: ...increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and climate shocks may cause disruptions in service delivery...

gen_risks.description: The new digital Employability Portal and upgraded LMIS risk underutilization or power disruption, mirroring past unoperationalized labor observatory systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt a cloud-based architecture, procure backup power systems, and contract specialized technical assistance for system development and user training.
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D Subcomponent 1.2: ...an 'Employment Observatory' was previously developed with support from the ILO but never fully operationalized...

gen_risks.description: Dominance of low-productivity informal firms in STP limits the domestic private sector's structural capacity to absorb interns into permanent wage jobs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Combine internship schemes with self-employment startup grants, productive inclusion packages, and MSME growth support.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.A Country Context: Micro and small enterprises make up 92 percent of all firms in STP... Most are household-run and provide few job opportunities.

gen_risks.description: High youth emigration sentiment (68%) without legal structures may result in uncoordinated brain drain or precarious irregular migration outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate structured labor mobility orientation sessions, align skills with destination country demands, and support formal international labor mobility channels.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.B Sectoral Context: A recent survey found that 68 percent of youth are considering leaving the country in search of better opportunities abroad...

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
